body:
[R85] POSITIVE - exact head e0c2fe08c798cf38d2f14af094fd8498ca971a19 Independent review round R85-4 of PR #428 (issue #413), cleared context, five lenses, every lens re-covered at this head because `scripts/gen_toc.py` is in every lens's scope and changed in the round-5 commit. Reviewed in a fresh public clone detached at e0c2fe08c798cf38d2f14af094fd8498ca971a19 (tree 12b6aa95a5625000846b7488d195737231e3d705), base 55518b470935f5478e0879bfc4ff183cc5d5ccc4 = `git merge-base origin/dev HEAD`. Five commits on the base: 1c31ffb0, b7114c23, f593dc7c, aab51d49, e0c2fe08 (review-evidence/head-identity.txt). Submodules present at the pinned commits: gptp-processor bacf8121, protocol-processor 2faa5af8, third_party/verilog-axis 48ff7a7e; `external` absent by design. The diff base..head is two files, `scripts/gen_toc.py` and `scripts/check_em_dash.py`, +387/-81 (review-evidence/diff-base-head.patch); the round-5 delta aab51d49..head touches `scripts/gen_toc.py` alone, +25/-27 (review-evidence/diff-r4-r5.patch), and `scripts/check_em_dash.py` is byte-identical to round 2 (sha256 4d638c96931cb2ed8f0581c26853c740c0019339 ee6dbcee72511d2189f6c58c). `scripts/gen_toc.py` at the head is ea79069f11ed934653d7aaea27fb24088bea13e7de95761069531b519b1d0872, 997 lines. Every artifact named below lives under review-evidence/ in this checkout and was produced here. The one tracked file I mutated (21 bounded reversion controls, `scripts/gen_toc.py`, one at a time) was restored from an in-memory pristine copy after every control, with its sha256 and `git status` checked before the first, after each and after all (review-evidence/reversion-controls.log, integrity.txt); `git status --porcelain` shows `?? review-evidence/` and nothing else, and the working tree is the head tree 12b6aa95. ## What was read Issue #413 (objective, authority, the three acceptance lines) and its parent #378; PR #384's body for how the type-6 exclusion landed; CONTRIBUTING.md sections 5 and 6.1; AGENTS.md sections 6 and 7; docs/development/CODE_QUALITY.md rule 12; CommonMark 0.31.2 sections 4.2 (ATX headings and the optional closing sequence), 4.4 (indented code), 4.6 (HTML blocks, start conditions 1 to 7 and "Blocks of type 7 may not interrupt a paragraph"), 5.1, 5.2 and 5.4, and 6.6 (the tag grammar), with GFM 0.29 section 4.10 (tables); the exact diff base..head and the round deltas 1c31ffb0..b7114c23..f593dc7c..aab51d49..head; the executor's REVIEW READY report for this head and the PR body as updated for round 5; the R85-1, R86-1, R86-2, R85-2, R85-3 and R86-4 reviews as published on the PR; the completed validation record for this head (comment 5643618191) and its replica appendix. GitHub's own Markdown rendering endpoint in gfm mode is the oracle throughout (review-evidence/oracle.py, responses cached in oracle-cache.json). Synthetic fixtures only: no repository content was sent and no public state was created. The author's tables and end-to-end rows were not taken as evidence; every number below is from a run in this checkout. ## Findings ```text [R85] SUGGESTION Tests - scripts/gen_toc.py:85 and review-evidence/mutant-P-reach.txt - the new `HEAD_RE` is held at its positive boundary and not at its negative one Requirement/evidence: 21 bounded reversion controls were applied to the tracked file and 20 are caught (review-evidence/reversion-controls.log). One survives both self-tests, 86/86 and 32/32: writing `(?:[ \t]*#+)?` for `(?:[ \t]+#+)?`, which drops the specification's requirement that a closing sequence be PRECEDED by a space or a tab (CommonMark 4.2). It is not an equivalent mutant. Over 16 probe shapes it changes 8 labels, and on three of them it is wrong where the head is right: `## Alpha#`, `## Sharp C#` and `## C# and F#` render with their trailing hash on GitHub and the mutant drops it. The shipped arm `a closed ATX heading` fixes the positive case (`## Alpha ##` listed as `alpha`) and no fixture holds the negative one. Impact: the reach is the Contents LABEL only. Every anchor is unchanged under the mutant, 0 of 16 shapes differ (review-evidence/mutant-P-reach.txt), so no link target moves, no exemption verdict moves, and the heading list of all 118 pages the generator owns is identical. A later edit of this expression in that direction would print a label that differs from the heading GitHub renders, with the link still resolving, and no gate would go red. No tracked page carries a closed ATX heading (0 of 159, review-evidence/corpus-census.txt). Required change: none for merge. Optionally one `keeps`-style fixture whose heading text ends in a hash with no space before it, so the boundary is held on both sides of the expression the round introduced. Verification: rerun review-evidence/revert.py; control P must be named by a failing arm instead of passing 86/86 and 32/32. ``` No BLOCKER, MAJOR or MINOR finding at this head. ## Clean lenses ```text [R85] PASS Conformance - review-evidence/matrix-base-vs-head.txt, e2e-exemption-head.txt, corpus-base-vs-head.diff - acceptance 1 to 3 measured against GitHub's renderer, not against the author's tables [R85] PASS RTL - review-evidence/rtl-lens.txt - every tracked object outside scripts/ is byte-identical between the base and this head, submodule pointers included [R85] PASS Robustness - review-evidence/probes-grammar.txt, probes-round5.txt, declared-residue.txt - the tag grammar, the indentation bounds and the malformed-input behaviour against CommonMark 6.6 and the renderer [R85] PASS Tests - review-evidence/reversion-controls.log, new-arm-coverage.txt, control-inventory.txt - every new fixture fails under the reversion of the classification it claims, and the #378 control corpus is intact [R85] PASS Docs - review-evidence/docstring-claims.txt, docs-lens.txt - every falsifiable sentence of the walk's docstrings holds, and CONTRIBUTING 6.1 still states the rule that is enforced ``` ### Conformance Acceptance 1, at the walk. A 68-shape predecessor matrix, each shape put directly above a lone `` wrapping `## Old`, judged against the renderer at the base and at this head (review-evidence/matrix.py, matrix-base-vs-head.txt): the base AGREES on 17 and INVENTS a heading the page renders nowhere on 51; this head AGREES on 63, WITHHOLDS on 5 and INVENTS on **0**. The five withholding rows are an indented ATX heading, an empty ATX heading, a heading inside a block quote and the two setext forms; all five are headings `headings()` has never listed, and the base withholds exactly the same anchors (review-evidence/withhold-residues.txt), so none is introduced here. The two flat-container residues the PR body declares by name reproduce as declared and are withholding-only (rows W6 to W8 of the same artifact). Acceptance 1, end to end through the gate. 26 shapes driven through `check_em_dash.judge()` on scratch repositories, the Contents block written by `gen_toc.apply()` so provenance really holds and the exemption is really asked (review-evidence/e2e_exemption.py, e2e-exemption-head.txt): 26 of 26 answer what the renderer says the base page shows. The twenty shapes where GitHub renders no such heading are refused with `mirrors no heading`, 1 finding and 0 exempt, the round-5 interrupting-item and closed-heading shapes among them; the six where it does render stay exempt. No row falls back to the prose message, so provenance held on every one. The reading. Round 1's "opens only after a blank line" is gone: the walk tracks a paragraph state and `_opens()` reads the tag only while none is open, which is the specification's own rule, and the matrix above is what that buys. Asked directly whether it can hide a heading that renders: yes, in the five pre-existing shapes and the three declared flat-container shapes, all withholding, which refuses a label rather than exempting one. A contributor sees that at once; it cannot grant the exemption #413 closes. Ownership and scope. `scripts/check_em_dash.py` grew no second walk: it imports `TOC_ENTRY_RE`, `generated_block`, `headings` and `label` from the generator and carries one regex of its own, a diff hunk header (review-evidence/docs-lens.txt). Its whole diff against the base is four hunks, the new type-7 control and the `_unwrap()` helper the type-6 control now shares, with that control's name and fixture text unchanged (review-evidence/diff-check-em-dash.patch). The rule, the provenance basis and the CI base derivation are untouched: outside `scripts/gen_toc.py` and `scripts/check_em_dash.py` every tracked object is identical, CONTRIBUTING.md and `.github/workflows/docs.yml` and `scripts/ci_events.py` included (review-evidence/rtl-lens.txt). Acceptance 3's last clause, reproduced rather than trusted. A per-page dump of `blocks()`, `headings()` with anchors and `generated_block()` over all 159 tracked Markdown pages, at the base and at each of the five heads: the base against this head diffs to 0 lines, and so does every intermediate head (review-evidence/dump_corpus.py, corpus-base-vs-head.diff, corpus-r4-vs-head.diff). The census says why: 0 type-7 tag lines, 0 closed ATX headings, 0 footnote definitions and 0 type 3 to 5 openers in the 159 pages (review-evidence/corpus-census.txt). The round-5 change itself. 22 closed-ATX probes against the renderer, label and anchor (review-evidence/probes-round5.txt): this head disagrees on 0, the round-4 walk on 13. The shapes that are NOT a closing sequence survive correctly, `## Alpha#`, `## Alpha #bar`, `## Alpha ## bar` and `## Alpha ##more` among them, and collision numbering is fixed with it (`## Alpha ##` then `## Alpha` is `alpha`, `alpha-1` here and `alpha-`, `alpha` at round 4). At the label level end to end, the round-4 walk writes an entry targeting `#old--heading-`, an anchor the rendered page does not carry, and this head writes `#old--heading`, which it does (review-evidence/closed-atx-e2e.txt; the gate verdict in that artifact's round-4 row is the head gate judging a round-4-rendered block, so the label and anchor columns are the meaningful comparison, not the verdict column). ### RTL The lens has no matching file in the diff and the artifact that makes it so is a tree-wide object comparison, not a path list: `git ls-tree -r` at the base and at the head differ in exactly two blobs, both under `scripts/`, and every other tracked object, the four submodule gitlinks included, is identical (review-evidence/rtl-lens.txt). No HDL, no pin or constraint file, no workflow, no suite inventory and no `.gitmodules` entry moves. The paths dev itself moved since the base are listed in review-evidence/merge-candidate.txt and none of them is `scripts/gen_toc.py` or `scripts/check_em_dash.py`. ### Robustness 45 tag-grammar rows against the renderer, each candidate line placed where no paragraph is open, asking whether a type-7 block opens (review-evidence/probe_grammar.py, probes-grammar.txt): 45 of 45 agree. Covered: bare open and closing tags, the self-closing form with and without a space, unquoted, single-quoted, double-quoted and valueless attributes, attribute names with a colon, a dot and a leading underscore, names with digits and hyphens, uppercase names, a name starting with a digit, a closing tag carrying an attribute, a space before the name, trailing text, leading text, trailing spaces and tabs, one, three and four spaces of indentation and a tab, the type-1 and type-6 names excluded by ordering, an unterminated tag, an unfinished attribute value, an unbalanced quote, two tags on a line, a comment, a processing instruction, a declaration, a CDATA opener, autolink and email shapes, a backtick in an attribute value and a bare `<>`. 20 interrupting-item rows (review-evidence/probes-round5.txt): 0 disagreements at this head, and 0 at the round-4 walk as well, which confirms what the round-4 review said, that the shipped behaviour was already right and only the arm was missing. Bullets `-`, `*`, `+`, ordinals with `.` and `)`, ordinal 0, 2 and 10, the empty forms, one to four spaces of indentation, a tab after the bullet, a lazy line, a second item and a fenced item content are all in the set. The residue the PR declares out of scope, measured rather than accepted: an unterminated type 3, 4 or 5 opener and a type-1 name that ends its line keep a heading the renderer shows nowhere, 7 rows, and every one of them behaves identically at the base (review-evidence/declared-residue.txt). The PR body declares this family and both earlier rounds agreed to leave it to a follow-up; nothing here makes it worse and no tracked page carries it. ### Tests Each new fixture fails when the classification it claims is reverted, run as mutants rather than read off the arm names (review-evidence/new-arm-coverage.txt): `interrupts = False`, the survivor the round-4 review named, now fails the three interrupting-item arms, FAIL 83/86; dropping the item content test fails the empty-item control, 85/86; putting the round-4 `HEAD_RE` back fails the closed-heading arm, 85/86. Each of the five new arms is killed by at least one control, and the full ledger of 21 controls, their exit codes and the arms each names is in review-evidence/reversion-controls.log. Both self-tests were run under every control and the file was restored from memory each time, sha256 equal before the first, after each and after all. The #378 rounds 4 to 8 corpus is intact: all 27 planted controls of the base are present at the head under their own names, with one added, the type-7 twin of the type-6 wrapped-heading control; none was dropped or renamed (review-evidence/control-inventory.txt). The two the round asks about by name are there and green: `mirrored label of a pre-existing heading passes`, the legitimate mirrored label, and `a fence marker in an old comment refuses nothing`, the page once wrongly refused. They are load-bearing: reverting the paragraph guard drives `check_em_dash.py --selftest` to exit 2 naming its type-7 control three times, and controls C, D and G drive it red too. All 86 shipped fixtures were rendered through the renderer and compared with `headings()` (review-evidence/arms-vs-github-head.txt). 84 agree on the whole heading list. The two that do not are the setext-underline predecessor arms, where GitHub emits an `

Alpha

` that `headings()` has never listed at any revision; the type-7 property each arm actually asserts agrees with the renderer in both, and the executor's claim is stated over the `

` list, where it is exact. ### Docs 23 falsifiable sentences of the walk's docstrings and definition-site comments checked against the behaviour they document (review-evidence/docstring-claims.txt): 23 hold. That covers the three raw HTML kinds and how each opens and ends, "never under paragraph text", the flat container rule for an indented line under a list item, a block quote, a footnote definition and a table row, the fence precedence and info-string rules, `_table_cells`'s counting examples, `_paragraph_after`'s statement about which items interrupt a paragraph and the `HEAD_RE` comment citing CommonMark 4.2. One row printed FALSE on my first pass; it was my own expectation of the label convention for the blank line that terminates a block, corrected in the same artifact, and the docstring is right. CONTRIBUTING.md 6.1 is untouched at this head and still states the rule that is enforced: the provenance-bound exemption decided from the headings of the base page, with "a raw HTML block" named without a type, which stays true. No other documentation page states the block-type rule in words the change makes wrong (review-evidence/docs-lens.txt). ## Earlier rounds' findings: closed or not Each answer below is from a run at this head, not from the PR body. - **[R85] F1 and [R86] F1 (round 1, at 1c31ffb0), MINOR** (the paragraph-interruption guard: a type-7 block after a heading, closing fence, thematic break, comment close, list item, block quote, table row, setext underline or type-1 closing tag still granted the exemption): **CLOSED.** All nine predecessors are INVENT at the base and AGREE at this head in the 68-shape matrix, and all nine read `refused, nothing exempt` end to end (rows R1-1 to R1-9, review-evidence/e2e-exemption-head.txt). Reversion control A, the round-1 reading restored, gives FAIL 55/86 and drives the gate to exit 2 on its type-7 control. - **[R86] F2 (round 1), MINOR Tests** (the type-1 ordering, the three-space indentation allowance and the self-closing form with no arm): **CLOSED.** Controls D, E and F each fail exactly one arm, 85/86, and D also fails one gate control. - **[R86] F1 (round 2, at b7114c23), MINOR** (a pipeless GFM delimiter row and a footnote definition left a paragraph open): **CLOSED.** Matrix rows for `:-:`, `---:`, the three-space row, the footnote definition, the interrupting footnote definition and the lazy line after one are all AGREE at this head; rows R2-1 and R2-2 are refused end to end. Control H, the pipe demanded again, fails the three pipeless-row arms, 83/86; control J, the footnote read as text, fails the three footnote arms, 83/86. Judged against the renderer: the mirror-image rows, a delimiter row whose cells do not match its header row's, stay exempt, as GitHub keeps those headings. - **[R86] F2 (round 2), MINOR Tests** (the pipe condition and the `^ {0,4}` indentation with no arm): **CLOSED.** Control H is named by three arms and control E by the four-space list-item arm. - **[R85] F1 (round 3, at f593dc7c), MINOR** (the indented-code opener gated on the previous line's blankness): **CLOSED.** Control G fails eleven arms, 75/86, naming the eight indented-code arms and the three tag-indentation arms, and drives the gate to exit 2. Matrix rows for an indented line under a heading, a closing fence, a thematic break and a list item, and end-to-end rows R3-1 to R3-3, agree with the renderer here and escape at the base. - **[R85] F2 (round 3), MINOR Robustness** (`TABLE_DELIMITER_RE` admitting a pipeless row indented four spaces or a tab): **CLOSED.** Control I fails the two indented pipeless-row controls, 84/86, and the four-space and tab rows stay exempt end to end, as the renderer keeps those headings. - **[R85] SUGGESTION (round 3), the 1000-line module ratchet: TAKEN.** 997 lines, `long module: 10 <= 10`, `scripts/py_idiom.budget` untouched and nothing moved out of the single-owner walk. - **[R86] F1 (round 4, at aab51d49), MINOR Tests** (the clause that lets a list item interrupt a paragraph had no arm, so `interrupts = False` survived every arm and reopened the escape for six shapes): **CLOSED.** I ran the mutant: FAIL 83/86, named by the three new interrupting-item arms. The second edit the finding named, the content test dropped, is now named by the empty-item control, 85/86. The six shapes it reached are AGREE at this head and at the round-4 walk alike (rows L1 to L6, review-evidence/probes-round5.txt), which is what that finding said. - **[R86] SUGGESTION (round 4), the closed ATX heading: TAKEN**, and renderer-confirmed on 22 probes plus the label-level end-to-end row. - **[R85] SUGGESTION (round 4), the mixed-comment shape named in the limitation list: NOT TAKEN.** The PR body still names the two flat-container residues and the types 3 to 5 family and not this one. The behaviour is unchanged and withholding-only at this head (review-evidence/mixed-comment-shape.txt), the round that raised it wrote "Required change: none for merge", and a suggestion does not affect coverage. Restated here so the ledger is not read as if it had been folded. - **[R85] SUGGESTION (round 1), HTML block types 3 to 5 and a type-1 name at the end of its line: NOT TAKEN, by agreement, still present and pre-existing** (review-evidence/declared-residue.txt, 7 rows identical at the base). ## Lens ledger | Lens | Covering round | Head | | --- | --- | --- | | Conformance | R85-4 | e0c2fe08c798cf38d2f14af094fd8498ca971a19 | | RTL | R85-4 | e0c2fe08c798cf38d2f14af094fd8498ca971a19 | | Robustness | R85-4 | e0c2fe08c798cf38d2f14af094fd8498ca971a19 | | Tests | R85-4 | e0c2fe08c798cf38d2f14af094fd8498ca971a19 | | Docs | R85-4 | e0c2fe08c798cf38d2f14af094fd8498ca971a19 | All five lenses are covered clean by this round at this head, with no BLOCKER, MAJOR or MINOR left open under any of them. The one SUGGESTION is optional by definition and does not affect coverage. ## The validation record, personally assessed I ran the documentation-side gates myself in this checkout at this head and every one exits 0 with the string the record and the REVIEW READY report claim (review-evidence/gates-head.txt): `gen_toc.py --selftest` PASS 86/86, `--check` OK at 101 pages, `--verify-anchors` 80 cross-page fragment links reproduced, `check_em_dash.py --selftest` PASS 32 arms and `--base 55518b47` 0 findings with arms 32/32, `docs_check.py` 0 findings across 159 pages, `ci_events.py --check` OK at 1030 contract items and `--selftest` PASS at 443 arms, `check_py_idiom.py` with every ratchet within budget and none moved, its self-test 54/54, `check_hygiene.py --check` PASS, `check_doc_paths.py` OK at 693 cited paths and `check_doc_style.py` OK. The hosted required contexts at this exact head are as the record reports: I queried them myself and the rollup is 20 SUCCESS and 1 SKIPPED, with `rtl-fast`, `verilator-suites`, `yosys-portability`, `elaborate`, `docs-check`, `docs-check-no-git` and `wire-accountability` all green (review-evidence/pr-checks.txt). One line of the record is now stale and I state it because the record rests on it. "The head descends directly from the live dev tip, so its tree is the candidate merge tree" was true when the record was written; `refs/heads/dev` is now 8019c9abc7bf232646963b75f5f36d2437d65ca5, five commits ahead of the base, so the head tree is no longer the candidate merge tree. It does not weaken the record. The merge base is still 55518b47, `git merge-tree --write-tree` produces 5af259ed2fd37a4f06fda887852704639fa90988 with no conflict, GitHub reports the request MERGEABLE and CLEAN, and that tree carries this head's two blobs unchanged (review-evidence/merge-candidate.txt, merge-tree-blobs.txt). Those five dev commits touch a workflow, the gPTP submodule, testbench and builder sources and several documentation pages, and none of them touches either changed script. I materialised the candidate merge tree and re-ran the gates on it: `gen_toc.py --selftest` 86/86, `--check` OK, `--verify-anchors` 80, `check_em_dash.py --selftest` 32 arms and `docs_check.py` 0 findings over its 159 pages, and the per-page classification dump over that tree is identical under the base walk and the head walk, 0 pages differing (review-evidence/corpus-merge-tree.txt). So acceptance 3's last clause holds on the tree that would actually merge, not only on the head tree. What I did not re-run, and why it does not block: the native bank, the local workflow replica and the full Yosys bank are RTL-side and outside this round's means. Their relevance here is as a no-regression baseline, and the diff reaches no HDL, no workflow, no constraint and no suite inventory (review-evidence/rtl-lens.txt), while the exact-head hosted contexts above carry the same claim independently. I take the record's gate evidence as sound for this head and for the candidate merge tree. R85-4 FINISHED
